syntaxRef.sectionTitle: Clasificación de Errores: Python vs JavaScript

rows.syntaxError: Parser fails before bytecode generation, halting immediately when def, if, for, or class headers are missing a trailing colon.
rows.logicTrap: Execution proceeds, but code runs outside its intended block scope, silently leaking state between branches.

rows.syntaxError: An uncaught SyntaxError halts the entire script thread, typically triggered by an unexpected token or unterminated string literal.
rows.logicTrap: Loose equality and type coercion let "42" + 1 evaluate to "421" without ever throwing, destabilizing downstream math.

faq.sectionTitle: Reglas de Puntuación, XP y Progresión

items.q: How is my bounty score calculated?
items.a: Each correct fix pays out a base bounty plus a speed bonus. Draw a fix in under three seconds and you earn the Dead-Eye multiplier, stacking your payout until you miss or time out.

items.q: What is XP and how do I earn it?
items.a: XP accrues per cleared snippet, scaled by difficulty tier. Logic traps and recursion bugs pay more XP than a first-outpost colon fix, rewarding engineers who tackle harder badlands.

items.q: How does the streak combo work?
items.a: Consecutive correct draws build a combo multiplier shown in the HUD. One wrong holster trigger or a blown timer resets the streak back to one, so steady accuracy beats reckless speed.

items.q: What happens if the timer runs out?
items.a: A timeout counts as a missed draw. Deputy Rusty stalls in place, your streak resets, and the correct fix is revealed in the telegraph explanation so you can study it before the next outlaw.

items.q: How do I rank up in sector progression?
items.a: Clearing all duels in a sector unlocks the next stretch of desert. Sector difficulty escalates from Semicolon Gulch through Canyon Recursion, introducing harder error classes as Deputy Rusty advances.

hero.titleLine1: El Duelo de Código en el Polvo de Neón:
hero.titleHighlight: Donde la Sintaxis se Encuentra con la Justicia Fronteriza
hero.description: Syntax Sheriff es una arcade de codificación interactiva construida para ingenieros principiantes que abordan Python y JavaScript moderno. Aquí, depurar no es una búsqueda oscura en documentación, es un enfrentamiento rápido de alto riesgo donde los errores son forajidos y cada corrección precisa mantiene el núcleo de vapor del Diputado Rusty pulsando hacia adelante a través del desierto.

lore.subtitle: Un autómata implacable de latón y silicio que atraviesa ocho tierras baldías fronterizas letales, impulsado exclusivamente por ciclos de compilación limpios y sin errores.

rusty.name: Diputado Rusty
rusty.description: Forjado en los silicones abandonados de Dodge City, el Diputado Rusty funciona con una cámara de batería inductiva que no puede quemar combustible fósil. Su tren de engranajes solo pivota hacia adelante cuando un ingeniero analiza correctamente la sintaxis defectuosa. Una respuesta incorrecta desencadena un estancamiento de tormenta de polvo, mientras que una compilación precisa enciende sus pistones de vapor y lo envía otro paso a través del cañón.

items.name: SECTOR 1: SEMICOLON GULCH

items.name: SECTOR 2: INDENTATION RIDGE
items.desc: Python four-space scoping, tabs versus spaces collisions, and nested function alignment.

items.name: SECTOR 3: DUSTY LOOP BASIN
items.desc: Off-by-one boundary traps, infinite while-condition flags, and break-statement short-circuits.

items.name: SECTOR 4: CANYON RECURSION
items.desc: Base case omissions, stack overflow badlands, and unreturned recursive branches.

items.name: SECTOR 5: BRACKET HOLLOW
items.desc: Mismatched curly braces, unclosed parentheses, and bracket-type confusion traps.

items.name: SECTOR 6: ASYNC MESA
items.desc: Missing await keywords, unhandled promise rejections, and callback ordering ambushes.

items.name: SECTOR 7: SCOPE LEAK CANYON
items.desc: Variable hoisting traps, shadowed outer scopes, and global leakage from unscoped assignments.

items.name: SECTOR 8: DODGE CITY VAULT
items.desc: The final marshal exam blending every prior syntax trap into one last high-noon duel.

options.note: Adds the required colon to open the block.
Semicolons don't open Python blocks.
Parentheses alone don't satisfy the colon syntax.

snippets.explanation: Python block headers like if, for, while, and def always end with a colon before the indented body starts. Without it, the interpreter can't tell where the block begins.
snippets.rule: Missing colon after a conditional header

options.note: Closes the parenthesis before the block opens.
Swaps the wrong bracket at the wrong spot.
Drops the opening parenthesis entirely.
Still never closes the condition's parenthesis.

snippets.explanation: Every opening parenthesis in a condition needs a matching close before the block's curly brace opens. This snippet closes the brace but never closes the parenthesis, so the parser can't find the end of the condition.

options.note: Increments count so the loop eventually ends.
Leaves count completely unchanged.
A comparison, not an assignment, so nothing updates.
Prints a value but never changes it.

snippets.explanation: The loop condition depends on count, but the body never changes its value, so the while condition stays true forever. Incrementing count each iteration lets the loop eventually exit.

snippets.consoleError: Warning: assignment used as a truthy condition

options.note: Compares by value and type instead of assigning.
Fixes the assignment but still allows loose type coercion.
Still an assignment, just with different capitalization.
Inverts the logic entirely.

snippets.explanation: A single '=' performs assignment, not comparison. The condition always evaluates truthy because the assignment itself returns the assigned value, so every caller is treated as a sheriff. Use '===' to compare by value and type.
snippets.rule: Assignment operator used instead of comparison

options.note: Extends the stop value so 5 posts are built.
Still produces only 5 values, now mislabeled from zero.
Skips every other post with a step of 2.
Identical to the original buggy line.

snippets.explanation: range(1, 5) stops before 5, producing only four values: 1, 2, 3, 4. To get five posts numbered 1 through 5, the stop value must be 6, since Python's range always excludes its endpoint.
snippets.rule: Range stop value excludes the final number (off-by-one)
